tasks.title: A card for one record
tasks.description:
Fill in `RecordCard` in `src/RecordCard.jsx`. Keep the named export `RecordCard`. It takes one prop, `record` (an object like the ones in `src/stock.js`), and returns one card:

- an `<article className="record-card">`
- the record's `title` in an `<h3>`
- the `artist`, the `year`, and the `price` written with `formatPrice` from `src/format.js`

Every value comes from `record`; nothing is typed in by hand. The check renders your card on its own with records it picks, and also looks for `<RecordCard` in `src/StockList.jsx`.
nextSteps: Copy the markup of one card from `App.jsx` into the return of `RecordCard`.
Replace each typed-in value with the matching field of `record`.
Import `formatPrice` and use it for the price.
hints: A component is a function that receives its props as one object. `{ record }` in the parameter list pulls out the one you need.

Inside JSX, curly braces switch back to JavaScript: `

{record.title}

`.
Leave the Sold mark out for now or copy it as it is; the third task is about it. Each value that was typed in becomes `{record.something}`.

tasks.title: Every record in the stock, from the data
tasks.description:
Fill in `StockList` in `src/StockList.jsx`. Keep the named export `StockList`. It takes a `records` prop (an array) and returns a `<ul className="stock-list">` with one `<li>` per record, in the order of the array, each holding a `RecordCard`.

Give each `<li>` a `key` that belongs to the record itself (its `id`), not to its position, so React still knows which item is which when the order changes.

Then make `App` render `<StockList records={stock} />` with the `stock` from `src/stock.js` in place of the hand-written cards. The check swaps in a different stock and expects the screen to follow it, with no key warning in the console.
nextSteps: Put a `key` on the element you return from `map`.
In `App.jsx`, import `stock` and replace the hand-written list with `StockList`.
hints: JSX can hold an array of elements, so mapping data to JSX is how a list is drawn from data.
The `key` goes on the outermost element returned from the `map` callback, here the `<li>`.
The index from `map` changes when the order changes. Each record already carries something that never changes.

tasks.title: Sold only when it is sold
tasks.description: Every card says Sold, but most records are still in the racks. In `RecordCard`, show `Sold` only when `record.sold` is `true`. A record with `sold: false` has no mark and no word Sold anywhere on its card. The check renders sold and unsold records on their own and then looks at the whole screen with a stock it picks.
nextSteps: Find where the card draws the Sold mark.
Look at the Browser panel: only two of the shop's records should be marked.
hints: JSX does not have an `if` inside it, but an expression can decide what to render.
`{condition && ...}` renders the span only when the condition is true.
React renders nothing for `false`, `null` and `undefined`, so `record.sold && ...` is safe for a boolean.
